name: ULTRAKILL
supported_versions: Per the adopted upstream converter: (1) the original Windows build used during development (the user's existing CrossOver copy) and (2) Steam depot 1229491 manifest 22957324. It verifies required game files and REJECTS other versions; every game update needs a new 'verified patch pack'. Newer-version-only changes (portal/blood patches) are applied only for the newer depot; older builds read disabledComputeShaders from LocalPrefs.json.
status: in progress: native arm64 + Metal, menu and tutorial render at 3024x1898 ~120 fps; campaign playthrough not yet verified; installed build keeps compute effects (palette LUT) on the CPU fallback; Steam init OK, overlay/cloud untested
approach_differences: translates shaders to Metal 2.2 (HLSLcc plus HLSL decompiler/vkd3d/SPIRV-Cross for recovery)
compiles the game's Burst routines for arm64+x64
patches managed code with Cecil (Windows memory-layout accesses, blood decals, portal clipping)
replaces Windows chess engine with a universal Stockfish
known_issues: Metal 'Vertex attribute TEXCOORD4 of type int2 cannot be read using MTLAttributeFormatUShort2' -> fixed by declaring Master vertex input as uint2 and as_type<int2> at use (1232 variants)
Intel path only tested via Rosetta
lessons_for_toolkit: vertex inputs whose mesh format is an unsigned/short type must not be declared as signed int in MSL (generic HLSLcc post-pass candidate)
keep CPU-filled lighting buffers enabled when compute effects are disabled
AssetBundles also contain shaders: patch bundles, not only data files
toolkit_usage: The port copied tools/ unchanged (inject.py, inject_inplace.py, xlate_all.py, metalsub.py, dxbc_rdef.py were byte-identical to this repo) and added only tools/patch_bundles.py (now upstreamed here).

The final app was produced by the adopted upstream converter, not by this toolkit: it has its own shader 'upgrade' passes on the translated MSL (color-output ABI, texture dimension queries, transparent/fixed (inline) samplers, clip distances for portals, recovered cage shader, unsigned light indices) plus Burst arm64 compilation and Cecil patches - game-specific, but several are generic repair classes (see docs/PIPELINE.md 'Open problems').

compute.verified_2026_11_21: all 5 kernels compile; ComputeLUT 512/512, CreateMask 64/64, Composite 64/64 texels match CPU references through Unity 2022.3.29f1's player on Metal (disposable clone, copied profile); JFA/Composite1PX not dispatched
compute.gameplay: the game's palette code (ConvertPaletteToLUT.ConvertPalette) dispatches the converted kernel without engine errors; visual parity unverified because the automated Level 0-1 baseline renders nearly black even with compute off; gameplay outlines use shader blits, not OutlineCompute; 2026-11-21: the user confirmed the installed app renders Level 0-1 normally, so the dark baseline is a test-harness problem (camera pose / capture), not a build problem
compute.next: fix the automated capture (pose, timing, which camera is read) or compare by hand: a separate copy with the converted palette kernel enabled, played side by side with the installed app, before installing
